sections.content: You know all of these forms: *ir a* + infinitive (A1), the simple future (A2 Unit 19) and the present subjunctive after hopes (A2 Unit 27). A connected account moves between them: plans, predictions, wishes and conditions.

items.spanish: Voy a salir temprano porque mañana tendré que trabajar.
items.english: I'm going to leave early because tomorrow I'll have to work.

items.spanish: Espero que el viaje sea tranquilo, aunque creo que habrá algún problema.
items.english: I hope the trip is calm, although I think there will be some problem.

items.spanish: Si todo sale bien, alcanzaremos la meta en un mes.
items.english: If everything goes well, we'll reach the goal within a month.

items.spanish: Estamos a punto de empezar, pero todavía no sabemos cuánto durará el recorrido.
items.english: We're about to start, but we still don't know how long the journey will last.

sections.content: Notice how these four sentences use four different forms, each answering a different question: *voy a salir* (a plan), *espero que sea* (a wish), *alcanzaremos* (a prediction that depends on a condition) and *estamos a punto de* (something about to happen).
